note: Twenty-four original two-speaker reconstruction tasks with fixed frames and machine-readable chunks. Some author-created banks include one unused chunk; the official example does not establish a universal distractor rule. One-point practice, not a complete timed Writing section. No per-item time limit inferred. All drafts await independent academic review.

questions.subject: Writing
questions.learningObjective: Order supplied words and phrases into a grammatical contextual response.
questions.prompt:
Speaker A: What do you need to find out about the lecture?
Speaker B: Do _____ _____ _____ _____ _____?

Arrange the supplied chunks to complete Speaker B’s reply. Keep the fixed words and punctuation. Use each selected chunk once; some banks contain an unused chunk. Do not add or change words.
Chunks: [when] | [the lecture] | [starts] | [does] | [you] | [know]
questions.answer: Do you know when the lecture starts?
questions.explanation: An embedded question after know uses statement order, not direct-question inversion.

sentenceAssembly.context: What do you need to find out about the lecture?

questions.practiceScoring: One original practice point; automated checks reconstruct the designated answer but do not establish linguistic uniqueness or ETS score equivalence.
